decisions.rationale: The relation language refuses every cardinality spelling the storage lowerer does not implement, and the surviving singleton cardinality="manyToOne" keeps its obligation: an axis narrowed to one value stays represented, so narrowing can no longer delete a shape from this record. The remaining observed relation obligations are still declaration and lowering evidence, not execution evidence, and remain explicit coverage debt until the sibling corpus supplies receipts. Join eligibility is deliberately NOT narrowed here: it is still accepted with zero consumers, is a known ADR-0041 violation left open on the record, and is owned by row lang-retire because every checked-in release entry has already serialized it. Re-derived again by 5g3-sm-impl over the ledger that already carries U5b's disclosure tier. The v5 cut adds 107 obligations, none of them observed, so this decision's obligation set is unchanged in membership; it is re-recorded because a decision is bound to the ledger it was reviewed against, and that ledger moved. Re-derived by LANG-ADOPT-v5, and this time the membership DID move: adoption swapped exactly 4 relation-scope obligations, the v5-valued node versions on $.relations[], .foreignKeyActions, .sourceEntity and .targetEntity replacing their v4-valued pairs. Nothing else entered or left this set, so no relation shape gained or lost coverage; only the version each one is observed at changed.
decisions.revisitCondition: Replace this decision with execution or stable-refusal receipts from the sibling relation corpus; any change to the exact observed relation obligation set, including widening the declined cardinality axis or retiring join eligibility under lang-retire, invalidates this decision immediately.

decisions.rationale: The whole-language ledger intentionally precedes execution coverage outside relations. This set now also carries the single-valued authored axes the earlier cardinality filter dropped, which are declared constants rather than choices; admitting them is an inventory correction, not a claim that any of them executes. Existing first-party uses are named evidence debt, not baselined as correct behavior, and this exact-set decision cannot absorb a new value or axis. Amended by U5b: this set now also carries one obligation from the surface-slot disclosure-tier axis — `$presence="absent"`, observed because every shipped slot omits the tier. The axis is admitted here as an inventory correction, exactly as the single-valued axes above were; no shipped slot declares a tier, so nothing about the tier itself is claimed to execute. Its other four obligations sit under the unused-shape decision. Re-derived again by 5g3-sm-impl over the ledger that already carries U5b's disclosure tier. The v5 cut adds 107 obligations, none of them observed, so this decision's obligation set is unchanged in membership; it is re-recorded because a decision is bound to the ledger it was reviewed against, and that ledger moved. Re-derived by LANG-ADOPT-v5, and this time the membership DID move: adoption swapped exactly 57 obligations here, every one a v5-valued node version replacing its v4-valued pair. Nothing that is not a version value entered or left, so no shape gained or lost coverage. Amended by profile-v2-adoption, which is the packet ADR-0047 s4a deferred U5b's declaration to. Exactly TWO obligations entered this set: $.surfaces[].slots[].disclosureTier.$presence="present" and ="always", both now first-party because party_detail's keyFacts slot declares always. Nothing left. This completes the disclosure-tier axis to three observed of five; the remaining two, ="onDemand" and ="progressive", stay under the unused-shape exemption and are U5c's question, not this packet's. Unlike every prior amendment here, this one is NOT an inventory correction: the declaration reaches a compiled artifact, because the same packet adopts compiler-semantic profile v2 and the tier is emitted only under v2. That is the whole reason U5b was told to move it here rather than mint an entry whose feature reached nothing.
decisions.revisitCondition: Each later language-axis packet replaces the corresponding obligations with execution or stable-refusal receipts; any change to the exact observed non-relation set invalidates this decision immediately.

decisions.rationale: These derived values and topologies have no first-party instance. Their exemption is conditional on remaining unused and is not evidence that the platform honors them. Re-derived again by 5g3-sm-impl over the ledger that already carries U5b's disclosure tier. The v5 language cut (ADR-0050) adds 107 obligations and all of them land here: one node-version value on each version-bearing authored axis, plus $.languageVersion="v5" and its paired normalization profile. They are unobserved for a structural reason rather than an accidental one -- node-version purity is uniform within a package revision, so no module can be authored at v5 until every module is, and ADOPTED_LANGUAGE_VERSION deliberately stays at v4. This exemption expires by construction at adoption, which is what the revisit condition below already specifies. Re-derived by LANG-ADOPT-v5, which is the adoption the paragraph above said would expire this exemption -- and the expiry was PARTIAL, which the prior record did not anticipate. Of the 107 obligations the v5 cut added here, 61 became observed at adoption and 46 did NOT, because they sit on axes the first-party corpus does not instantiate at any version; they were unobserved at v4 for that reason and remain unobserved at v5 for the same one. The 61 that moved out were replaced one-for-one by the v4-valued obligations they superseded, so this set is the same SIZE and a different SET. The 46 that stayed are the substantive ones: nine are $.stateMachines[] axes and one is $.operations[].effect.transition, which no product module can observe until a product state machine exists -- PUR-1, not this packet. The rest are predicate and filter nesting depths, quantity base units, storage evolution and promotion, and the surface renderer. Their exemption remains conditional on remaining unused. Re-derived by profile-v2-adoption. Two obligations LEFT this set -- $.surfaces[].slots[].disclosureTier.$presence="present" and ="always" -- because party_detail's keyFacts slot now declares the tier, which is the first first-party occurrence this decision's revisit condition names. The exemption expired exactly as written, and partially: ="onDemand" and ="progressive" remain, and their exemption is unchanged in both membership and reason. onDemand is refused by name in normalization because this application is server-rendered with no fetch-on-expand behaviour to honour it; progressive is refused because U5b emptied its allow-list rather than add a fifth predicate, and the authority for it is owed by U5c. Neither is unused by accident, and neither may be un-exempted by authoring a specimen -- that would ship a spelling ahead of its meaning, which is the ADR-0041 s3 rule that kept toast and modal refused.
decisions.revisitCondition: The first first-party occurrence changes the observed partition, invalidates this exact-set decision, and requires execution, stable refusal, or a new explicit ruling before the gate can pass.
